#3966. PSA: Xbox And GTA 6 Have Both Pushed Out Small New Updates

One's a console update, the other potentially a "day one" patch

As we get ready to wrap up the working week here at Pure Xbox, we wanted to alert you to a couple of new updates that have been pushed out in recent days - one for Xbox consoles in general, and another specifically for GTA 6.

The Xbox console update was actually released on Wednesday, but nobody made a song and dance about it whatsoever, while the patch notes only referenced "general stability and performance improvements".

However, we now know that the update was related to the addition of achievements in four original Xbox games, and unless you download the update, you won't be able to see those achievements right now.

There's a chance your console may have downloaded this automatically but to check, go to "Settings", "System", "Updates" and then see if there's an update waiting to be downloaded or not.

News Four OG Xbox Games Are Getting Achievements For The First Time Ever

"We’re introducing one of the top requested features"

As for GTA 6, in addition to the 200GB+ preload that went live a few days ago, there's also now a new update as of a few hours ago that sits at around 2.2GB. You'll need to download this in order to start playing on November 19th.

Some people are speculating that this might be the so-called "day one patch", but who knows whether we might get another one between now and next Thursday. In any case, you'll want to get this queued up as soon as possible (unless you haven't installed the game yet, in which case it'll be included in your initial download).

There's a chance you may see a different size, but it's somewhere around that 2.2GB mark. We're also spotting that some people haven't got it yet for whatever reason, but it should roll out to all Xbox users in the very near future.

Don't forget that Alpha Skip-Ahead Xbox Insiders have also received a special new update this week that adds three new features for testing purposes, so if you're part of the Insider programme, keep an eye out for that.

We'll be back next week with loads more coverage on the GTA 6 launch, and here's hoping there are no more downloads to get us ready for November 19th. Just a few more sleeps until the big day!

#3965. Star Wars: Galactic Racer Reaches 1.5 Million Players, Teases Future Updates

Developer Fuse Games has announced its debut title, the brilliant Star Wars: Galactic Racer, has amassed 1.5 million players.

The news comes via a recent social post, featuring the one and only Biddy Blas himself:

It's unclear if the number equates with sales or is purely the number of people that have logged in, but either way, it's a pretty impressive milestone for the arcade racing title.

Galactic Racer has amassed this amount of players in a little over a month, when it launched to an overwhelmingly positive reception.

Its relentlessly fast racing, silky smooth controls, and moreish roguelike structure made it all stand out, and speaking personally, it's easily one of my favourite games of 2026. I wrote about it recently, and used it as an excuse to mention Burnout far too many times.

Anyway, the post also suggests the team is not done with Galactic Racer yet. Fuse Games says it "can't wait to share more about the future of Star Wars: Galactic Racer", which is a very exciting prospect.

Many are hopeful for additional locations and courses, even more abilities and perks for build variety, and features like creating custom events. I'd love for all of this to be added eventually, but for now we don't know exactly what the team's plans entail.

#3964. The Legend of Khiimori's Mongolian Expanse update brings in frosty mountains and scorching deserts that'll require a lot more than a fur coat and a sturdy horse

Another day, another opportunity for some horsing around! I'm being literal here, to be clear, as a new update for The Legend of Khiimori dropped yesterday. It's called The Mongolian Expanse, opening up the map a whole lot more and making a sweep of other additions to the game.

Previously, you might have looked out unto the snowy mountainscapes and the scorching deserts and thought "boy howdy am I glad I can't go there, those temperatures look like a nightmare to deal with!" Well, good news, as you now can head to those locales, each with "their own waystations, Yam nodes, named places, chests and bandit caches."

You don't want to wander there without some amount of prep, however, as the mountains are cold and difficult to climb, with wolves none too kind to humans like you. The desert, of course, is really hot, for both you and your horse. Both additions remind me of Zelda: Breath of the Wild and its use of extreme temperatures acting as a sort of challenge gate. Neat stuff!

The buck doesn't stop there with this update though. You'll find a whole host of new wildlife, ranging from wild boars, to gobi bears and camels. Of course, a horse game wouldn't be one without more horse, which there is! It's a new breed called the Marwari, a horse that is "built for endurance and especially resistant to heat, a strong partner for long, punishing Desert crossings." Beyond that, you'll also find more than 60 new horse skills, all findable across specific regions and for specific breeds.

It's a nice beefy update with plenty more tweaks, additions and fixes on top of everything mentioned above. When it comes to the mountains and desert, you can also expect some big additions there, as this is only the first part of this update. You can read about everything else the update offers right here on Steam.

#3963. After a 16-year long dev period, Faraway, a shooting star arcade game about siphoning the energy of other stars, is out now

Lord almighty, video games take a while to make, 'ey? Especially if you're just one person working on it by yourself. Such is the case with Faraway, out today, an arcade game that reminds me of the early days of PS3 indies "about a shooting star that creates constellations to stay alive," all made single-handedly by creator of cult-classic mobile game Eliss, Steph Thirion. Did I mention that Faraway took 16 years to make? Like I said, game development is a lengthy process.

Looking at Faraway, and knowing how long it took to produce, it doesn't surprise me to come from a dev who managed to release a mobile game in the early days of the platform, long before free-to-play got its chokehold on the industry. It also really does feel like it should be sitting amongst the likes of PixelJunk, this thing should be something I'm desperate to play on my PS3 while I wait for my controller to charge.

As mentioned, you are a shooting star, a "spark meant to shine and vanish in a blink." But still you persist, connecting to and wrapping yourself around starts to "harvest their energy," in turn lengthening your own life, and of course, in arcadey fashion, racking up a nice score. It looks like game design as poetry, everything you're looking at procedurally generated to bring freshness to every run. I can fully envision this as a "one more run" kind of arcade game, the best kind, especially in an age long past the need to shove in another of your hard earned coins.

Faraway conceptually charms me because it taps into a style of game we don't get to see much of any more. What I'm saying is, I'm just a teensy bit sick of how many roguelikes there are, but that doesn't mean I don't want a game I can just hop in and out of at my own whims. Sure, arcade games might not be in vogue, I just miss them a bit. In any case, Faraway is available to pick up on Steam right now. Seems like it'll be worth a punt!

#3962. Kevin Feige says Doctor Doom isn't a variant of Tony Stark

Join the GamesRadar community for quick access. Enter your email below and we'll send confirmation, and sign you up to our newsletter.

Keep exploring and earning more as a member.

Avengers: Doomsday hits theaters in a little over one month

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Kevin Feige says Doctor Doom isn't a variant of Tony Stark... despite that confusing Avengers: Endgame Encore post-credits scene making us think otherwise.

"People wondered, ‘Is Doom just a variant of another character? Is this just a shortcut to bringing back another character?’ The answer is no. He’s Victor Von Doom," Feige told Empire.

In one of several post-credits scenes that were added to the re-release of Avengers: Doomsday, Tony Stark is seen forging what appears to be a Doctor Doom mask. How are we not supposed to think that this implies Tony and Victor Von Doom are one and the same (aside from being played by the same actor)?

Even Variety posed a theory a little while ago that Doctor Doom is a variant of Iron Man from another planet, but it must be said again that Victor Von Doom and Tony Stark are completely separate characters in the comics. They go head-to-head in the 2008 comic book Iron Man: Legacy of Doom (which Downey was seen reading as part of his Doomsday prep). I hear you, though: How is the movie going to explain away Tony Stark and Doom having the same face? Well, he's rarely ever unmasked in the comics... so I just kind of figured the Russos were going to rely heavily on that. We'll see come December.

Avengers: Doomsday hits theaters in the UK on December 16 and in the US on December 18. For more, check out our guides to the Marvel timeline and how to watch the Marvel movies in order.

#3961. Ablahshikar is a maximalist, sickos only salvage-survival CRPG about ripping organs out of warships and pawning off strange goods that's now out in early access

I don't know what's going on, and I like it

Sometimes, you come across a game and instantly know it's for the sickos. Today that is Ablahshikar, a "turn-based salvage-survival CRPG adrift on the Candle Sea" where you rip out the organs of enemy warships to "rebuild your vessel into a doomed chimera," that is out now in early access. To be honest I could have just called it a CRPG and still labelled it as a game for sickos, yet everything that's going on here is obviously just doubling down on the sick factor.

Ablahshikar is a particular flavour of maximalism. Having not played it, it feels a bit impossible describe, I mean, just have a read of some of the game's Steam page: "Lo, destiny crooks a finger only to those whose eyes peer beyond þe next tempest. Take custody of a faltering war-barge that wanders the outer brine of Dastgerd. Thy wrists y-braced to a wan terminal of bone-whyte and tarnysshed latoun, þou steerest Ablahshikar by murke point-nettes and sputteryng tables." I don't know what any of that means! And I love it. Reminds me of Hylics in that the game's world is not translating itself for its audience; you take what you're given, and you figure it out yourself.

Judging from trailers and screenshots, there's a mix of activities to be getting on with. Occasionally you'll be piloting a strange, not alien, but definitely ancient ship of some kind in an arcadey sort of fashion. Then occasionally there's something that resembles Caves of Qud, i.e. some odd, 2D maybe dungeon crawling where your moves are dictated by individual keys on your keyboard. Then there's Disco Elysiumy cutscenes that feel like a video game designed in the year 1200 by someone from the year 2200, aesthetically anyway. As I said, it is a particular flavour of maximalism.

Truthfully, I do not know if I am sicko enough for Ablahshikar. Its mighty vision is terrifying, but I certainly am curious about it. Right now it's less than a fiver, and it'll only be in early access for roughly a couple of months where the price will then go up, so perhaps it's best to get in at the ground floor. If you are one such sicko, then you can pick it up on Steam right here.

Geoff Keighley has announced the nominees for all of the categories at The Game Awards will be confirmed next week, on 17th November 2026.

It's confirmed that GTA 6 will be eligible for all the awards, despite the fact the game won't launch until two days after it could be nominated for the top accolade. Other potential inclusions could be Control Resonant, Phantom Blade Zero, or The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time — depending on how the jury feels about including remakes.

#3959. BioWare are gone, but at least you'll be able to watch their final days in a documentary next year and oh wait that's really sad actually

It feels like every single week for the past few years has been the infinitely quotable 30 Rock quote on repeat. That feeling struck particularly last month when EA decided to shut down the iconic Mass Effect and Dragon Age developer BioWare. That obviously resulted in the cancellation of Mass Effect 5, of which a leaked trailer and some, now former, devs made sound pretty interesting. But hey! At least there's a documentary coming next year all about the studio that managed to capture the studio's last days! Yeah, I'm not so convinced by this upside either.

As reported by Deadline, Shane Fennessey and Adam Scorgie will be helming a documentary about the beloved RPG studio for Canada's Super Channel. It's called, punnily enough, Massive Effect: The BioWare Story, and will apparently take a look at its origins in 1995 all the way up to its closure and a bit beyond, planned for release in 2027. Filming began two years ago, so clearly this was meant to be much more of a celebratory project than the funeral procession it's going to be.

Some big names from BioWare's history will be appearing in the doc, including its founders Ray Muzyka, Greg Zeschuk and Augustine Yip, alongside the likes of longtime devs like Mark Darrah, David Gaider, Drew Karpyshyn, Aaryn Flynn, Mac Walters, Trent Oster, James Ohlen and Caroline Livingstone. You can also expect appearances from Jennifer Hale, Casey Hudson and, as if his sole goal is to haunt this industry everywhere, Geoff Keighley.

In a statement, co-founders Muzyka and Zeschuk said, "When the production team asked for our blessing to tell the BioWare story, we were honored and deeply moved. BioWare was never just about the logo or the building. It was about the stories brought to life by the amazing people on our dev teams, and the fans who defended those worlds, championed them and carried them forward. We’re proud this film honors those who made it all possible. The best stories never really end. They live on in our memories and wait for someone to pick them up again."

Obviously the documentary won't only be about the studio's closure, it sounds like a much bigger effort than that, so hopefully it will be a way to recognise how much of an influence BioWare has had on RPGs. It's just a ridiculous shame that it's something of a posthumous release. Continued solidarity with all those at BioWare.

#3958. Three Classic Startup Animations Are Set To Arrive On Xbox Very Soon

They were mentioned in some recent patch notes

So, you remember that recent Xbox console update we mentioned yesterday? The one that happened on Wednesday and included original Xbox achievements? It seems like there's at least one more hidden feature to be discovered.

A couple of eagle-eyed Xbox fans have spotted that the patch notes had been adjusted for this update last night, and they mentioned that three classic startup animations were being added to "celebrate 25 years of Xbox history".

The three animations are for the original Xbox, Xbox 360 (2005) and Xbox 360 (2010).

Since then, the patch notes have been adjusted once more to just reference "miscellaneous" improvements, so it seems like they jumped the gun slightly and were supposed to wait until November 15th (the date of Xbox's 25th anniversary) to reveal these three startup animations.

None of them are live yet by the way, but it might be worth checking the "Startup" section of your Xbox console's Settings menu periodically over the next couple of days to see if they show up.

I don't know about you, but I'm going to be rocking the original Xbox startup animation as soon as possible!

Robert Downey Jr. is teasing something rather cryptic over on Instagram... and we're thinking it has to be the final Avengers: Doomsday trailer.

In the video, which can be viewed below, Downey is standing in a green sweater... kind of looking like he's up to no good. While he doesn't say anything in the video, the caption reads: "Patience, subjects... Time will tell. Doom won’t..."

Empire Magazine dropped the cover story for their special Doomsday issue, and teased that something else was arriving at 4 PM tomorrow (though this could be 4 PM BST, as Empire is a UK-based magazine), and we have a feeling that it may very well be the final Avengers: Doomsday trailer ahead of the film's December 18 release.

A post shared by Robert Downey Jr. (@robertdowneyjr)

Because the promotion for Doomsday started with a bunch of "special clips" before we got a proper trailer, tomorrow's trailer might be something out of the ordinary as well. We still don't know what the movie is actually about, although the Russo brothers confirmed to Empire that he is indeed the villain of the movie, and that even though he's got some trauma... we should definitely be scared of him. I mean, did you see that VisionQuest episode 8 post-credits scene? He resurrected an entire Avenger from the dead... for nefarious reasons, of course.

Avengers: Doomsday hits theaters in the UK on December 16 and in the US on December 18. For more, check out our guides to the Marvel timeline and how to watch the Marvel movies in order.

Tae Kim, author of The Nvidia Way, thinks there are some promising alternatives to Huang.

There is also one excellent external candidate who has been very successful outside of Nvidia and offers both technical expertise and solid business management experience. Employees loved working for him. Either one would be great.November 11, 2026

We thought it might be coming, and it's here: Jensen Huang is no longer CEO of Nvidia, as he has resigned following an admitted affair, and an additional alleged one.

It wasn't unexpected, and both before and after the announcement there has been a lot of talk about how it would be a bad decision and could spell very bad news for Nvidia. And, well, there's certainly some truth in that given we saw company share prices drop after reports of Huang's alleged second affair came to light.

After perusing X for a while today, the general sentiment seems to be that Huang was so incredibly central to Nvidia that the company couldn't possibly do well without him. Or at the very least, nowhere near as well as it would with Jensen sticking at the helm. Ditto the AI market in general.

But not everyone agrees. In fact, one of the most credible voices on Nvidia reckons there are "strong" and "excellent" candidates for a replacement. Tae Kim wrote the most well-known, authoritative book on the company—The Nvidia Way—and yesterday they explained:

"Many people have cited my book as saying Nvidia would be completely lost without Jensen Huang. My views have evolved in the several years since I wrote those passages. I now believe there is a strong internal candidate with the technical expertise, experience, customer relationships and respect of employees needed to lead Nvidia effectively into its next chapter."

"There is also one excellent external candidate who has been very successful outside of Nvidia and offers both technical expertise and solid business management experience. Employees loved working for him. Either one would be great."

They're certainly optimistic comments, but your guess is as good as mine as to who they might be referring to—presumably someone on the list of potential replacement CEO candidates I put together earlier.

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products

We now know that the actual interim CEO is Colette Kress—exactly who we predicted it would be. I'm not sure whether that's who Kim had in mind, given they decided, for some strange reason, to not mention who they were thinking of by name. But if not, there's still room for the next proper CEO to be one of those he has in mind.

This being said, Jensen Huang's status, drive, and deep familiarity with the company and the market are undoubtedly unparalleled. I think you'd find it difficult to pin down anyone who could reasonably disagree with that. In which case, while Nvidia might not be "completely lost", it's hard to say it will be as oriented as it would be with Huang still at the helm.

#3955. Take on a time-manipulating corporation in the very Soul Eater meets Jet Set Radio action roguelite CHRONO PUNK

Plus a little bit of Spider-Man, Devil May Cry and Kingdom Hearts

My favourite kind of game that's obviously going for the vibe of a particular era of gaming is one that doesn't look like it's trying to be any other game from said era, moreso if someone told me it was a PS2 or a Dreamcast game everyone forgot about I'd believe you. CHRONO PUNK fits that vibe quite well, an action roguelite that looks like it's taking some cues from those aforementioned consoles, alongside the likes of Soul Eater, Jet Set Radio, Devil May Cry, and Spider-Man.

That is, obviously, a lot of things, but CHRONO PUNK on the surface appears to have its own identity at least. Your player character looks like an almost nightcore version of Sora Kingdom Hearts, with various roles and weapons to choose from; there's a sword and shield, pistols, shurikon, grimoire, and most Soul Eatery of all, a scythe. CHRONO PUNK's got vibes, too. The cities you do combat in are big and nondescript when it comes to details, but ripe for jetting about and Spider-Man-style swinging across the place. And besides, it looks like there's some hub areas ripped straight out of any stylised MMO from the 2000s.

I'm liking the look of the combat too. This'll obviously be one for the combo pilled out there, people who like to bounce back and forth between their enemies like a pinball. Slow paced, this is not. Sick, I hope this is. Pair all of that with some bouncy, wall running movement, and there's some real potential for a strong game here. Sounds like you'll be able to play it in co-op or solo too, which is a nice touch.

The story doesn't seem all that complicated, with some mega corporation manipulating time thereby controlling the city and the masses, leaving you to deal with the mess, but hey, I'm here for the vibes. As of right now, there's no release date attached to CHRONO PUNK, but you can wishlist it on Steam while you wait.

As the Editor of Push Square, Sammy has over 15 years of experience analysing the world of PlayStation, from PS3 through PS5 and everything in between. He’s an expert on PS Studios and industry matters, as well as sports games and simulators. He also enjoys RPGs when he has the time to dedicate to them, and is a bit of a gacha whale.

Donkey Kong Bonanza and look outside before GTA6

God of War (2018) Now I understand why people talk about it so much and why it's held in the highest regards. Everything blew my expectations out of the water. The voice acting was incredible and some of the best I've heard in any game, the visuals impeccable, and the score sounded and felt so powerful. The combat had such perfect flow and I felt like a real warrior, no other game has made me feel that way before. Then there was the story, so phenomenal. Today I listened to the novel of the game read by Mimir himself, all nine-hours of it (Alistair Duncan is the perfect narrator) and I wasn't playing Barbies Rewind as I listened oh no. I was pumping up my hours in what is now one of my favourite digital dopamine delivery systems.

I jumped on the game the second it went live, then after a while (eleven-hours) had to stop so I could give God of War the attention it deserved (and because I was told to go to bed) Now I can once again heed the Emperor's call to purge the Tyranid filth from the universe. It might look like a Vampyre Survivors reskin, it's not. There's so much more to the game, multiple troops onscreen, chainswords, boltguns, bit-boxes, paint pots, power-ups and more dangerous enemies. There are all kinds of lore accurate characters/classes and the tools needed to get the job done. It feels so good to stomp around the battlefield in a suit of armour reducing hordes of monsters to ash while additional troops shoot and cleave their way through with me.

My favourite characters so far are Brother Luca Amasius (boltgun) and Captain Tor Garadon (he rains down rockets everywhere) I may have also bought a couple of Warhammer sets too, and some books but that's a hobby to try for another day. I have some Warhammer audiobooks ready to go for future runs too, the Nightlord books were recommended. Another game launched on the same day, it too is of the dopamine delivery genre.

My first coin pusher game feels more like a drug pusher because once again there's all of that dopamine. Addiction is a strong word, but I can say that yes this game is incredibly addictive and I've never played anything like it. You take control of a greedy little panda who has a thing for shinies and uses a coin pushing machine to get that fix. It's chaotic, there are literal money trees, all kinds of passive perks, flashy quirks. It's all in the name of good fun and in getting those higher numbers. It's the perfect little 'one more run' game.

Continuing to play the GOTY Phantom Blade. I’m about 25 hours in and adoring it. Story is there and very good if you don’t mind reading.

To break it up I may dip back into Valor Mortis or Control Resonant, but my time is set for the next few months. I’ll be skipping GTA6 at launch as I remember 5 being good, but not generational for me.

I played Zero caliber 2 on the dead again psvr2 headset on ps5. It is pretty much cod with ps3-ps4 level graphics, but pretty good VR mechanics. Guns have a lot of attachments. They can be picked apart and reassembled (maybe a shotgun with silencer and zoom scope is not particularly useful in reality, but its video games after all ...). In terms of gameplay I would rank it above cod because of the very well implemented VR mechanics. Some of the levels are very good, some of them a bit barren. The cut scenes and dialogues are forgettable, and that is presumably the area in which the budget difference is most obvious. Other negatives: the game is not necessarily super well balanced. For me the upgrades improved and then leveled off too quickly, and enemy encounters lacked a little bit of variety. Also I had the impression that approaching enemies silently did not really change anything. The most significant shortcoming for me was the 3D audio implementation. Either the problem is that voices are not muffled by walls, or there is no 3D audio at all. Anyway it is difficult to localise enemies by sound. So clearly there is room for improvement. But in case You search for something for Your dead and dusty psvr2 and You are into such kind of games a very good pick.

Then I jumped into tetris effect and slip vector on psvr2 for a couple of minutes. I am not so sure about the "game" in split vector, but in terms of visual effects both games are delivering for me, and split vector is (or was) on a steep sale.

@Gremio108 Exactly it looked like a knock-off of something like No Man's Sky so I skipped it for so long. @4fold I can't imagine five or so hours of dealing with those space bugs, you obviously mean with breaks I hope. Raccoin is a weird but fun game, the first time I tried I didn't get it. I suppose that's how people become addicted to real-life gambling machines, it's the essence of 'just one more try'.

The appeal for me is about learning. It allows me to hold up a mirror and understand how humanity can be corrupted. I see 40K less as glamorizing dehumanization/brutality and more of a reminder. Most people go through life without seeing either, I think it either makes you, breaks you or you lose yourself to something else. I want to learn from it. I can trace everything in those games back to real-life, genetic purity, industrialized extermination, dehumanization, genocide, xenophobia even thought crimes. There's the imagery/terminology, it's less of a fascination and more of a sobering observation.

#3953. Talking Point: What Are You Playing This Weekend? (November 14-15)

It's the penultimate weekend to get stuck into the games you'd like to finish before November 19th rolls up.

It's WAYP time, people! You know the score by now, so let's hear what you're playing this weekend! This is your opportunity to have a chat with one another about what's good, what's worth playing, why you're vibing, or maybe, not vibing with certain games. It's an open floor, PX'ers.

Alrighty then, let's get into it. Here's what we're playing on Xbox this weekend:

Recently, I haven't been trying to complete anything, grind online, or chase a Mythic cheevo. I'm just vibing with my Xbox. Honestly, I think GTA 6 has me in a bit of a chokehold, keeping me from starting anything I might not finish. With that in mind, Hozy has been the perfect lil' game to sit down and chill with on a rainy day.

Lots of games are getting little bits of my attention, including Silver Pines, TCG Card Shop Simulator, and Gears of War: E-Day, to name a few. But, my main game at the moment is It Takes Two. I've absolutely loved playing it with my wife. The best bit is how into it she is, that and the bonded trauma it inflicts!

Something I'd like to get back into is Marathon. That new Symbiosis trailer looked awesome, and I'm hoping to lock-in and get that Mythic. I think all I need is to grind to level 100 and it'll be mine. Shouldn't be too much of a time commitment, right?

But I'll be real. I'm playing a lot of Zelda: Ocarina of Time right now. It's a perfect remake of a childhood favourite, and it's feeding my inner kid. He's a happy boy.

GTA 6 is right around the corner, and you better believe it's going to take up the rest of the year in terms of dominating my free time. That means it's not really wise to get stuck into anything too meaty right now, although I'm keen to check out Shrek 2 Remastered and see whether Aspyr's new port does the OG Xbox title justice or not.

I might even play a bit of GTA: Chinatown Wars on my 3DS. I finally started playing that game about a year ago, and even though it's rough around the edges by today's standards, I'm enjoying how unique it is compared to other entries.

#3952. After taking over EA, Saudi Arabia and their private equity cronies have reportedly held talks about buying Unity

The engine builders have, it's claimed, been working with an investment ​bank to evaluate [their] options

Members of the consortium led by the Saudi Arabian government's Public Investment Fund and some private equity suits which took over EA this year in a leveraged buyout worth $55 billion reportedly have a new target in their sights. Unity, software company and makers of the game engine bearing the same name, have held talks with the consortium over a potential takeover, it's claimed.

According to Reuters, a consortium including Saudi Arabia’s sovereign wealth fund and private equity firm Silver Lake Partners recently approached Unity about a deal that would value the company at around $25 billion. Unity are, it's claimed, currently working with an investment bank to evaluate their options following the chat, with no deal set in stone right now.

Silver Lake, Reuters note, are already among Unity's largest shareholders and invested up to $400 million in the engine builders in 2017. In fact, Silver Lake's managing director and CEO Egon Durban already has a seat on Unity's board of directors, so will probably have to butt out of any takeover talks.

Assuming the consortium would go the leveraged buyout route, loading Unity up with debt like the EA takeover did, it's hard to see any deal not resulting in similarly catastrophic consequences for those working at Unity. EA laid off a reported 400 people in an effort to cut costs after coming under the boot of the Saudi state and private equity, shutting BioWare and cancelling something Sims-related codenamed Project Lotus. BioWare's demise has since been reported to have largely come down to EA execs not wanting to fund both Star Wars Battlefront 3 and Mass Effect 5, with them opting to back only Battlefront 3.

Unity's recent financial results are looking strong, propped up by year-on-year growth in an AI-powered ad network dubbed Vector, so one would assume that bit of the business likely wouldn't be top of the list if any bloodletting was to end up happening.

Solidarity to any Unity workers who're now having to live under the shadow of this prospective takeover and the upheaval it could lead to if it goes ahead in a fashion which mirrors the EA deal.

Asha Sharma says MachineGames "has done remarkable work" on Wolfenstein

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Wolfenstein 3 is officially in the works at MachineGames, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has announced.

Sharma has been firing off semi-big announcements via her official Twitter account all day in celebration of Xbox's 25th anniversary, including confirmation that Id Software is working on a new game, but this is undoubtedly the biggest news of the bunch.

"Wolfenstein 3 is officially in production at @MachineGames," reads a tweet from Sharma. "One of gaming's most important franchises, and a team that has done remarkable work bringing it forward. Looking forward to sharing more."

Not much else was revealed about the Wolfenstein revival, but it's exciting to know it's a full-blown mainline entry and not a spinoff ala Young Blood (which I enjoyed, to be fair). This will be the first mainline entry in the legendary first-person shooter series since 2017's Wolfenstein 2: The New Colossus, which somehow was almost 10 years ago.

Wolfenstein 3 is officially in production at @MachineGames. One of gaming's most important franchises, and a team that has done remarkable work bringing it forward. Looking forward to sharing more. https://t.co/YyX8LrbTvhNovember 12, 2026

Remember when I said "not much else was revealed" about Wolfenstein 3? Well, that's because Sharma was generous enough to tease us with a picture appearing to show the first page of Wolfenstein 3's dialogue script, seemingly confirming the first chapter is called Nazitraz. The scene opens in the inside of an interrogation cell with a conversation between longtime Wolfenstein protagonist William Joseph "B.J." Blazkowicz and a German-speaking character called Otto, which could be a number of bad guys throughout Wolfenstein history. B.J.'s longtime right hand, Fergus, also seems to be in the scene, but that's about everything that can be inferred based on what's shown.

MachineGames has been Bethesda's trusted Wolfenstein developer since 2014, starting with Wolfenstein: The New Order.

No details regarding platforms or release timing were revealed.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

The happiest time of year is just around the corner, folks. The PC Gaming Show: Most Wanted sponsored by Pot Noodle will be airing December 3rd, and we'll be counting down The Council's 20 most anticipated games.

There's one major change this year, though. We've gone from counting down the top 25 games to the top 20. We've made this decision to ensure each game gets its time in the spotlight, meaning the show will be more enjoyable to watch. Also, The Council have recently unionised and refuse to count more until we agree to give them bathroom breaks, which we simply will not do.

The Council remains, as ever, an inscrutable bunch of journalists, developers, celebrities, creators, streamers, gaming luminaries, and just generally people whose opinion on videogames carries some weight.

Each year, we knock our heads together and puzzle over how to whittle down the thousands of upcoming games into a list of just 100. Several factors go into this, such as how many wishlists a game has on Steam, how interesting a trailer is, the position of the stars at the time a game was first announced, and generally just how excited those of us at PC Gamer are for a title.

The full list awaits below, and the top 20 are nestled within it, but you'll never be able to figure out which ones they are. And if you do, please don't share your findings on the internet or you'll ruin the whole show. You'll notice there are fewer than 100 games, and that's because each year, some come out before the show or unfortunately get cancelled. Try as we might, we can't get The Council to predict the future—we'd all be retired by now if they could.

The Council gives each game they're excited for a score from one to five, with one being passingly curious to five being intensely, worryingly hyped. If a member has no interest in a game at all, they simply don't vote on it and that is counted as a zero.

We also take into account how many members of The Council voted for each game so that any with the same average score have a reliable tiebreaker. Some other factors go into the weighting, too, like if we've had no news about a game in a long time or, again, where the stars are and what they think of the whole thing.

#3949. "It's a brave new world": GTA 6's PC port will release sooner than you think to avoid losing money to AI rip-offs, says former Rockstar tech director

"If it's GTA, I think people are gonna try it."

GTA 6's PC release may come sooner than anticipated, according to former Rockstar North technical director Obbe Vermeij, because Rockstar and publishers Take-Two will be concerned about losing money to unofficial generative AI clones of the PS5 version, once it launches on 19th November. In general, Vermeij thinks that how to avoid having your games duplicated by chatbot herders is "the big question" right now for devs and publishers, particularly those who don't have the means to enforce their intellectual property dominions as vehemently as Take-Two do for Grand Theft Auto.

Speaking to me during a wide-ranging chatathon, Vermeij reflected on the early days of Grand Theft Auto development at Rockstar North in the 90s, and how the Noel-and-Liam-Gallagher-esque relationship between PC and console gaming has evolved. He shared a sweary anecdote about the company's difficulties getting the original GTA 1 to look the business on Sony's PlayStation.

"I didn't work on GTA 1 and 2, but I worked for the company at the time, and I was actually right next to the GTA 1 team, so I was able to follow it," he said. "So they worked on PC and then an external company in Dundee did the PlayStation version. Which was really weird, because like, PCs were so much more powerful - still the case, but in those days, it was even more so.

"And I remember, at the time, the GTA team was definitely the most rowdy of all of the teams," Vermeij continued. "And there was one particular day where they sent the PC build away, and then it came back from the PlayStation people, and they had cut down all the textures from 256 colours to 16 colours, and my god, the artist was just going around and swearing - 'what the fuck did they do to our textures, I can't believe it, we can't release this shite'. So it always has been that sort of awkward relationship between PC and the console. So in those days, it was like PC first and then console second, even though that didn't really make much sense for the sales, because the PlayStation versions sold way better."

When it came time to develop GTA 3, Rockstar "flipped that around", Vermeij went on, creating the console versions first. "Clearly the PC market has sort of grown, caught up with the console market, but there's still that same mindset," he said. Most publishers prefer to release all versions at once, Vermeij added, "because then there's only one marketing campaign they have to pay for." GTA lives by its own rules, however. "I guess it's less of an argument for them because the game is just so big, so they just kind of always left it that way. And for developers, it's way easier to just do one version at a time. So, you know, that makes sense."

The arrival of generative AI threatens to throw all this to the winds. Tools such as Reverse Engineer Anything allow for speedy unofficial ports or "slopcomps" of console games on PC, despite warnings from seasoned recomp developers that using genAI for this purpose wrecks the community aspect of unofficial porting, and results in illegible "bruteforce" code rather than preserving some understanding of how the original game was made.

"It really has changed the world," Vermeij observed, "and I think I would be concerned, if I was Rockstar, that somebody would just take the PS5 version and get AI to change it to PC, which won't be won't be as good as their effort, but it could still also hurt their sales. So, I wouldn't be surprised if there was an effort to get [the releases] a little bit closer together. Obviously, I don't really know what they're thinking."

GTA 6 is, according to Rockstar and Take-Two at least, an enormously fiddly production, costing hundreds of millions of dollars over eight years in development. Nonetheless, Vermeij thinks current genAI tools are "probably" capable of pulling off a port. "It will take a long time. It actually, physically takes hours and hours and hours to do these things. And it will take a bunch of tokens and everything, so it would probably cost like, tens of thousands of dollars in tokens. But like, you know, if it's GTA, I think people are gonna try it."

There are already signs that genAI PC port goldrushers are ready to pounce on GTA 6. Just today, Ars Technica reported on efforts to yassify the game's PS5 trailer footage by piping it through a stronker PC graphics card and using Nvidia's DLSS 5 to apply extra layers of gloss.

Vermeij himself left Rockstar way back in 2009 and is now an indie developer. His current early access project is Plentiful, a hexagonal god sim with an emphasis on water physics. It uses "AI-assisted machine translation for localization", but not for "gameplay content, art, or audio". Vermeij is, in general, interested in generative AI despite the surging tide of slopcomp ports. Smaller indie developers are, of course, more vulnerable to the financial fallout from having their work unofficially cloned by generative AI, but Vermeij thinks it's an existential worry for megacorps like Take-Two as well.

"I don't really see how you could protect against that, to be honest," he told me in closing. "I don't see it. But a big company like Take-Two, they would be able to get the lawyers on the case, and maybe, like, you said, for a big game, maybe the AI doesn't really do a particularly good job. But yeah, I mean, it's a brave new world. What was the case before, is that there's so much effort in developing the game, that it is not possible to rip it off, and that's completely changed now. So, yeah, we're going to have to see in the next couple of years, how that's going to pan out."

The latest rumour-mongering places GTA 6's PC release sometime in early 2027. In other news, Rockstar staff are soon to formally vote on whether to apply for union recognition. If the organisers carry the day, the resulting union could encompass nearly all the company's UK staff below management level.

#3948. GTA 6 PS5 Codes Potentially Being Stolen from Physical Copies Using Flashlight Trick

A potentially problematic manufacturing oversight may be resulting in some GTA 6 codes being stolen from retail PS5 cases.

Some reports claim that by pointing a strong flashlight at the side of the case, it’s possible to shine light into the empty Blu-ray box in such a way that it makes the code printed on the insert visible.

Remember, GTA 6’s physical release is a code-in-box, and doesn’t have a Blu-ray disc.

There is some debate about whether the included poster insert blocks the light and makes this impossible; some say they’ve been able to replicate the issue, while others say it can’t be done with a sealed copy.

It’s also worth noting that the US release specifically has a camouflaged pattern around the code, as shown by ResetEra user Mattmo831. That means you can certainly shine light into the box, but you can’t read the code on the other side.

Some PEGI units don’t have the camouflage pattern, so technically the code is visible using this trick, although again there’s still debate over whether the poster blocks the light in sealed copies.

It’s worth pointing out that codes aren’t activated at the point of purchase like other digital vouchers, so assuming the flashlight method works, it would be perfectly possible to pilfer a working copy of the game.

I think this story will explode if it turns out to be true, but it all just depends on how many PEGI copies don’t have the camouflage pattern and whether the inserted poster blocks the light or not.

As far as I can see, there aren’t an enormous number of people who’ve complained upon buying the physical version that their code has been redeemed – but if this method works, the publicity around it will now surely see the probability increase.

Avatar: Seven Havens season 2 gets a release date

Avatar: Seven Havens season 2 has officially set its release date, and it's not too far away. The Legend of Korra sequel will release Book 2 on May 21, 2027.

Just like the first season, there will be 13 episodes in total, and they will air in three-episode chunks through to June 11. The next stage of Pavi and Nisha's journey is called 'Book Two: Discovery' and the synopsis teases plenty more adventure yet for the twins.

This reads: "Pavi continues her chakra journey to the Floating Isles and learns more about what happened to Korra. Meanwhile, Nisha discovers vital information about the mysterious spirit energy Pavi released from Ellora. The girls are brought together in New Ba Sing Se, along with all their unresolved issues."

Saheli Khan returns as Pavi in the new episodes, alongside Aishu Devan as Nisha, Akshay Khanna as Karthik, Major Curda as Jae, and Sakina Jaffrey as Agam. Paramount also doubled down on the future of the show, confirming that Book 3 and Book 4 are also planned, with the former also airing in 2027.

Speaking to GamesRadar+, executive producer Ethan Spaulding teased the show's new location in Book 2. "I'd say get your surfboards," he told us, suggesting a rewatch of the finale. "I think if you guys freeze-frame, you can kind of get a vibe of what that haven might be like. But yeah, it's a fun place."

Avatar: Seven Havens Book One is out now on Paramount Plus. For what else to watch, check out our guide to the best shows on Paramount Plus as well as our round-up of all the upcoming TV shows you need to know about.

#3945. Steam gets a boatload of restored Wing Commanders and Ultima ports after EA producer stumbles across cupboard of old tapes

"He took me over there, opened it up and it was like Indiana Jones"

EA have stuck a bunch of restored versions and ports of classic games, on Steam, GOG and the EA App. 25 games in all, including multiple entries in the Wing Commander and Ultima series, are part of the haul. Why's this happening now? Well, an EA producer stumbled across a cupboard full of old tapes, film reels and CDs.

According to an interview with The Game Business, the discovery of this old gubbins was a consequence of EA senior producer Jim Vessella needing somewhere new to stick a bunch of Betacam tapes used to help make the Command & Conquer Remastered Collection. "One of the facilities people was like, 'I think there’s a room in the other building that has a couple of items like that'," Vessella recalled. "He took me over there, opened it up and it was like Indiana Jones… just, whoa. Knowing what I’d discovered with the Command & Conquer tapes, I really felt like we had to find out what was on all these tapes."

The producer was able to convince EA's bosses that this stuff was worth the work needed to stick it back on storefronts, and lo, an EA blog post gushing about their vault's door having slid aside to reveal this pile of retro games. The collection includes restored versions of the following games, all with "robust quality-of-life updates and higher resolution Full-Motion Videos (FMV) from the Master tapes":

Meanwhile, the rest of the lineup is filled out by "faithful ports" of the following:

On Steam, all of these are currently on sale for less than a fiver each, with the prices of the most expensive ones set to rise to just under £10 when the introductory offer expires on November 19th.

It's good news in preservation terms, though I'm not sure it totally washes away the bad vibes of EA's Saudi and private equity owners reportedly looking to take over Unity.

#3943. DokeV Set for 2028 Launch, But You'll See It Again This Year

But the Crimson Desert dev is embracing AI

Remember DokeV? The bizarre Pokémon-esque game announced over five years ago from Pearl Abyss? The developer has gone on to make Crimson Desert, but in a new financial report, it's shared its wild take on Pokémon is still coming.

Now its Charting the Unknown expansion for Crimson Desert is out, it's shifting more of its developers onto DokeV, and the firm is targeting a launch in the second half of 2028. Before the end of this year, however, it plans to reveal its latest "development progress".

DokeV was originally revealed at Gamescom Opening Night Live in 2021, a show run by Geoff Keighley. There is a good chance the re-reveal of the game will take place next month at The Game Awards, then.

Here's that wacky announcement trailer as a reminder:

Having shown it again, Pearl Abyss will have hands-on demos in the second half of 2027. It said: "We will continue to communicate with players by sharing updates at optimal timing to effectively highlight the game's direction and core strengths."

The problem is it sounds like the developer is embracing more AI development to achieve that.

In the financial report, Pearl Abyss confirms that it's "integrating AI technologies to enhance development productivity and overall quality". AI is being used across "the automation of repetitive tasks, content creation support, and test optimisation", and its use is being expanded to the team's "entire development pipeline".

"This enables a more efficient allocation of development resources and enhances overall production speed," it added.

News 'We Should Have Clearly Disclosed Our Use of AI': Crimson Desert Dev 'Sincerely Apologises' for Erroneously Including AI Art in PS5 Game

For now, though, the studio claims AI serves "strictly as a tool to support concept validation and pipeline productivity". Humans are still behind the "core gameplay experience and actual content creation".

Crimson Desert got into hot water shortly after its release for including AI portraits in some of its environments. It did remove them from the game and issued an apology where it said the assets were "unintentionally included in the final release. This is not in line with our internal standards, and we take full responsibility for it."

Now, as it looks to the future, Pearl Abyss seemingly plans to lean even more into AI development.

[source pearlabyss.com, via gamesradar.com]

#3942. Airframe Ultra's PS1 cyberpunk city is an amazing tribute to G-Police and WipEout, and I wish you people would slow down to appreciate it

But what if we could gawk at the dumpsters

I do not wish to "rule the streets" of Megacity West, dear creators of Airframe Ultra. I wish to be ravished by them, rubbing my face against the rusty corrugated metal of the shipping containers, and savouring the acid blue waters of the bay. I do not want to "become the one thing with freedom in a city of billions: A racer." I want to become the other thing with freedom in a city of billions: a person who slowly drives or – whisper it - walks around just looking at stuff, because gadzooks, this is one of the prettiest PS1 cyberpunk burgs I've laid eyes on.

Those eroded pastel chevrons. Those seductively wobbling vertices. That electric reef of a downtown backdrop, murderously luring your gaze from the on-coming trucks. That layer of invigorating crackle over everything. Every moment or so, I dismount from my hoverbike to inspect some concrete ruin I could swear I last saw in G-Police, or ponder the resemblance between a subway tunnel and WipEout 2097's Gare d'Europa. Then, somebody waps me in the skull with a stop sign at 300 kilometres an hour. But I was already stopped, frantic stranger! Your brutal poetic ironies are wasted on me.

Despite my best efforts, Airframe Ultra is a battle racer. It's co-developed by Videocult, the people behind Rain World – a game it looks nothing like, but is comparable to in the sense that there is an ocean of industrial refuse to navigate, and you will very often die. Each battle race is broken into sprints around a branching course that has been smashed together by the forces of urban decay. You will corkscrew down storm drains and barge through old abandoned clifftop mansions under a scarlet sun, zip along deadly flyovers and thread the barely legible layouts of high density slums.

Your hoverbike handles like a bronco full of helium, and that's before you start wanging it off the gloriously marbled, low-poly rubbish heaps that stud the city, shunting the game's camera through surfaces and exposing the map's underside in what the absolute squares amongst my readers will doubtless deem "an inelegance", but which true turbojunkeys will appreciate for its makeshift exuberance.

You've got a boost button which generally gets you exploded – and all that's before you get to the time-limited battle arenas that bookend each sprint. Here, players attempt to slaughter each other as much as possible, spending collectible cash on floating weapon pick-ups that range from bent pipes to Gatling guns and EMP grenades. Then it's off for another sprint. The first player to earn 10 points and place first in a subsequent sprint wins the match. I have not won many matches. My primary goal right now in Airframe Ultra is persuading everybody to stop and swap some emotes, while I coo over an amazing piece of graffiti I've found.

My efforts to make Airframe Ultra a walking sim aren't just about scenery. The game is surprisingly engrossing on foot, with some woozy tank controls that make me think of the experimental days before every third-person control scheme became a variation on Assassin's Creed, Uncharted or Gears of War. You have to hammer a button to run, for instance, and you'll wind yourself fast. You can also perform punches and kicks in four directions, with grander attacks to discover by smooshing together inputs. You'd best believe I burst into tears when I realised what this reminded me of: it's Bungie's Oni! The game with the finest martial arts system ever coded! There are more obvious influences, like Road Rash, but in these grim days of endless parrying, I'll take all the Konoko callbacks I can get.

Ahhhhh. But if only this had a proper single player mode. Online and local splitscreen with drop-in bot support are all you get. I wouldn't say Airframe is the most balanced deathracer, either. In my experience, and do bear in mind I mostly try to avoid the racing component, victory typically goes to whoever lands a fat cash reserve and grabs an AK47. That mild shambolicness is arguably part of the charm, in that it supplies incentive to stop and drink in the atmosphere. These streets are big and broken and beautiful enough for all of us, friends. Let us rule them together. Read more on Steam.

Despite being a late addition swap-in as Marvel's big new villain, Doctor Doom has now had the same number of appearances as Thanos. Before 2018's Avengers: Infinity War, Thanos appeared in two end-credit scenes for The Avengers (2012) and Avengers: Age of Ultron (2015), as well as in the story of Guardians of the Galaxy (2015), all setting him up as the MCU's big bad.

Marvel hasn't had the same luxury of time with Doom, as one Twitter user pointed out, after he was announced in 2024 following Jonathan Majors being axed as Kang. As a result, the studio has been speedrunning his introduction, including him in three post-credits scenes in just over a year.

His first silent appearance came at the end of Fantastic Four: The First Steps in July 2025, when he's seen speaking to a young Franklin Richards before Sue Storm walks in. His second two appearances saw him recruiting new team members for his nefarious plans.

In Avengers: Endgame Encore, he finds Bruce Banner being held in a prison post-Spider-Man: Brand New Day before taking him away. His most shocking appearance then came at the end of VisionQuest, when he resurrects Scarlet Witch, telling her that her power will be his.

Doctor Doom now has the same number of appearances as Thanos had before Infinity War https://t.co/Wm1EibapW0November 11, 2026

It's been a pretty quick turnaround of set-up for Doom ahead of Doomsday, but it does mean we have some insight into what he's planning ahead of the movie's December release. It seems he's been recruiting several powerful figures to help in his fight against the Avengers.

Marvel fans have been reacting to the appearances, and it's fair to say that opinions are pretty mixed. "Thanos sent the army & Loki on Earth in 2012, & was the presence looming over the entire Guardians of The Galaxy AND there were a ton of people that were connected to him & suffered a lot because of him, seeking him," one wrote on Twitter, adding: "Btw I'm not saying this to trash Marvel with Doom, I can't wait for Doomsday, but yes, I wish they had him felt more to build up the DEPTH of the hype."

Meanwhile another wrote: "Honestly, they handled the switch from Kang to Doom really well, given the obvious reasons for it." A third then tweeted: "Imagine if Doom was planned from the start: his face with the hammer sound in Endgame (2019), Wanda in Doctor Strange (2022), Loki visiting Steve and the TVA’s fear in Loki's series, Bruce's kidnapping in Spider-Man BND, All set up years ago instead of added later."

Avengers: Doomsday hits UK cinemas on December 16 and US theaters on December 18. For more upcoming superhero movies, here's our guide to new Marvel movies and shows on the way.

#3939. Terrific fantasy RPG Queen's Domain gets first proper update, adding a new throwing weapon and options to make puzzles "less frustrating"

Extremely good King's Field-style RPG Queen's Domain – or is it a Metroid Prime homage? Or a stealth Morrowind-up? We hacks simply cannot decide – has received its first proper patch, adding a hitherto "missing" throwing weapon, the Grave Knife, alongside a bunch of quality-of-life fixes.

They've stirred in the ability to disable screenshake, alongside some new icons to make status effects more obvious. They've also introduced "options to make some late game puzzles less frustrating", though they don't specify which. How frustrating! Still, it's a tidy overhaul for a game that has rapidly become one of my 2026 favourites.

The big mystery with the update is what the new Grave Knife does. You'll find it inside the Tower of Knowledge, once you've managed to unlock passage. As for those overly aggravating late game puzzles – I find the toughest part of puzzling in Queen's Domain is often just spotting switches and key objects, so perhaps it's something to do with that?

True, there's a large selection of skeleton tableaus who comically point the way to your next objectives, but the game's pixel aesthetics can be rather dense. I very much approve of this on the whole. I like how organic and tumbledown the environment feels - the repeated delight of realising that, yes, you can get over there, and wow, there's a whole other level down here.

Queen's Domain has earned a lot of happy reactions, and is a solid commercial hit. Developers Freshly Baked say it has sold over 100,000 copies, with Vertical Slice reporting that they've already broken even. Glad tidings indeed. Find the full patch notes below, via Steam.

With Jensen Huang stepping down from Nvidia amid a second affair allegation coming yesterday, Nvidia will be looking for a new permanent CEO, with Interim CEO Colette Kress taking over for now. There will no doubt be lots of names thrown out over the coming weeks, and current US President Donald Trump has joined the pile, insisting the AI company hire ex-Apple CEO Tim Cook.

Taking to Truth Social, he says, "NOW THAT Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place - TIM COOK of Apple. A Legend replaces a Legend!"

Tim Cook became the CEO of Apple on August 24, 2011, famously taking over for Steve Jobs, the founder of the company. Tim Cook stepped away from his seat as CEO in August, 2026, but has stayed on as the Executive Chairman of Apple.

Tim Cook and Donald Trump have had a longstanding professional relationship, with the ex-Apple CEO reportedly donating $1 million to the Trump inauguration. Trump brought both Jensen Huang and Tim Cook on his trip to China earlier this year, where they had negotiations with the Chinese government to open up trade relations in regard to AI hardware. This was the first presidential trip to China since Trump's first visit back in 2017.

Whether or not the 66-year-old ex-Apple CEO is the right man for the job, his relationship with Trump is undeniable, and they both seem intent on growing AI in America and supplying more (but a limited amount of) AI to China.

Nvidia is a company that owes its sudden net worth explosion to the widespread adoption of AI. It went from a company with a market cap of hundreds of billions in 2020 to a company with a market cap of trillions in 2026. It saw a stock dip this morning, but even at its lowest stock price in more than a year, the company's market cap is still close to $4 trillion. Apple, too, has grown significantly and is currently the most highly valued company in the world.

Tim Cook is just one of many names tipped to take over as CEO in the future, with some Nvidia staff such as current CTO Michael Kagan among them. But, as far as external candidates are concerned, one might consider Intel's CEO Lip-Bu Tan, AMD's CEO, Lisa Su, Arm's CEO Rene Haas or even Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk as potential candidates. The doors really are wide open.

#3937. I just found out you can use your Steam Wishlist to search for deals on games outside of Steam, saving my nephew more than £40 on Total War: Warhammer 3

It earned me a bucketload of uncle points

I may be very late to the party with this discovery, but I only just realised you can connect your Steam Wishlist to a third-party deals tracker. The beauty of which is that, once hooked up, you can see what games you've been pining for are going cheap not just on Steam but through any major shopfront across the internet.

I worry that I will be coming across as 'Use this one trick to save money – greengrocers hate it!', but it's already helped save my nephew more than £40. Even if it meant using a slightly underhand method.

Two weeks ago, I got a text from my nephew asking what the best way to play Total War: Warhammer 3. When I messaged back a couple of hours later (look, I'm not a responsive uncle) to tell him it's currently £50 on Steam, but it's worth waiting because according to SteamDB's price history it's come down to £7.50 in the past, I was too late. He'd got itchy feet and bought it at full whack on Steam, using up all his birthday money.

That's when I went looking and found Is There Any Deal for the first time. (A lot of you in the comments may be throwing your hands up in despair to hear this oversight) If you've not come across it before, it's a site that tracks game sales across loads of shops, including Steam, EA Store, Epic Games Store, GamersGate, GOG. GreenManGaming, Humble. This means while a game may not be on sale on Steam you can see if it's on sale anywhere else.

In the case of Total War: Warhammer 3, while it was full price on Steam, over on the Humble Store it was discounted to £7.49. I sent a link to my nephew and then told him, using the authority only an uncle has, that it's okay to refund the game through Steam and buy the cheaper version. It's not something I've ever done myself, but he's 17 and that is a lot of money to save.

Anyway, that's recommendation the first. It was only when I was looking for a way to export my Steam Wishlist to ask RPS supporters what I should cull that I realised Is There Any Deal has another feature: you can import every game on your Wishlist to get deal notifications. (This may get a second groan of despair in the comment section.) Once linked up, the site will ping you a notification whenever games you're waiting for pop up in a deal.

Just looking at my current list, I can get Genesis Noir, Ancient Enemy, and Norco for £10 total, all of which with more than 70% discounts through stores other than Steam. So, as you can see, this could be both a saving technically and lead me to spending a lot more money than I mean to…

You may already have heard of these tools, but as I hadn't I thought it best to give them a shout out.

Now considering I've revealed myself to be a rube, what other third party tools should I be installing to weaponise my Steam Library?

#3936. The Excellent Warhammer Survivors Reveals Roadmap Full of Free Updates, Teases Something Big

Warhammer Survivors launched just a few days ago, and I think it's an absolutely fantastic take on the criminally addictive Vampire Survivors formula.

Imagine my glee, then, to learn that developer Auroch Digital has big plans for the game going forward.

The Bristol-based studio has revealed a chunky content roadmap that leads into next year — and there's some really good stuff on the way.

It all starts with a major update that's landing in December. It'll bring new characters, weapons, and weapon evolutions to the already packed release.

Another two admittedly lesser but still welcome updates are expected in January; one promises quality of life improvements — which is interesting in itself — and the other will add cross-save functionality, so you can carry your progress between multiple platforms.

After that, a second major update drops in early 2027. Like the one that's expected in December, this patch flushes the game with yet more new characters, weapons, and weapon evolutions. You'd best get grinding before then!

And finally, at some point in the second quarter of next year, there's going to be a "larger piece of content". I'm guessing this'll be some sort of DLC or expansion; as of right now, Auroch Digital's teasing it and nothing more.

"We have been blown away by the support of Warhammer Survivors since launch, and we want to share our appreciation for everyone who has played the game so far," the developer writes.

#3934. Kevin Feige didn't want Wanda Maximoff to reunite with Vision in VisionQuest because the show should "stand on its own"

Join the GamesRadar community for quick access. Enter your email below and we'll send confirmation, and sign you up to our newsletter.

Keep exploring and earning more as a member.

Paul Bettany says they considered bringing Wanda back

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

VisionQuest came to a close with an epic season finale that saw Vision reunite with both of his sons, Billy and Tommy Maximoff. However, there was a missing member of the family: Wanda Maximoff. She's mentioned several times in the final few episodes but doesn't appear in the main series.

However, it turns out that they did consider bringing her back. Speaking to The Playlist, Vision star Paul Bettany said: "I remember having this conversation with [Kevin Feige], and he said, 'You and Terry [Matalas, showrunner] have done such a great job at making me care about Vision. I really don't think you should distract from that by giving the audience that at the end of the [show]. It will just fundamentally all become about WandaVision again, and this should and can stand on its own.' And I think he was right."

Of course, this doesn't mean that Wanda doesn't appear at all in the Disney Plus show. In the finale's second post-credits scene, Doctor Doom takes a trip to Mount Wundagore. We see Wanda pull down the mountain on top of her, as happened in Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness, before Doom appears and lifts the stones off of her. He brings her back to life before saying, "Scarlet Witch awaken, your power will be mine."

Elizabeth Olsen looks set to appear in Avengers: Doomsday then and a recent leak from Anthony Mackie seemed to confirm that Vision is coming back too. We may finally get a Maximoff reunion after all then, although probably not under the best of circumstances.

#3933. Real-time strategy game The Fertile Crescent 2 is an isometric odyssey inspired by Age of Empires, with the 1.0 release out now

Time to power-rank the biggest Bronze Age civs

Age of Empires-influenced real-time strategy game The Fertile Crescent 2: Collapse of the Bronze Age leaves early access today, publishers MicroProse have announced, with the 1.0 version adding the final chapters of the singleplayer story. You'll also get your grubby fingers on the very same map editor developers Wield Interactive used to design the campaign.

I'm new to The Fertile Crescent 2 myself. I do like the sound of a strategy sim in which you guide a fugitive community through the Late Bronze Age Collapse. The land has been thrown into turmoil by the arrival of the Sea People, this being a loose historical term for assorted ocean-going migrants who, I gather, are often blamed for the crumbling of the Hittites among other once-glorious Bronze Age powers. I don't have much scholarly insight to share - I thought the "Sea People" referred to expansionist mermaids, at first - but I do have a trailer.

Nate Crowley (RPS in peace) was exceedingly fond of the original game, calling it "a bite-sized chunk of phenomenal RTS design" that "manages to riff nostalgically on Age Of Empires, while completely rewriting its ground rules". The sequel continues with the same core concepts – above all, the paramount importance of food, which determines population and army size together with your civ's progression.

"This is not a game about building the biggest empire," the developers explain in a press release. "Resources have to be managed, stability is fragile, and growth comes with risk. Every expansion, every battle, and every decision must be weighed against survival. Building and managing a sustainable economy is as important as commanding your forces in battle. Expanding your army too quickly can put your food economy under pressure."

The story spans 17 missions, with four playable factions: the Assyrians, Egyptians, Babylonians, and Hittites. The 1.0 release also includes some standalone scenario missions, a skirmish mode, and multiplayer on dedicated servers with bot support.

Read more on Steam. If you're partial to historical strategy and don't mind winding back the clock (upturning the hourglass? Adjusting the sundial? Recalibrating the henge?) another few thousand years, Folk Emerging is pretty terrific. If you like stories about migrant tribes, and you don't mind trading your Hittites for Vikings, you might get a kick out of The Banner Saga.

With Jensen Huang gone, someone has to fill his boots. That's Kress, for the time being.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Jensen Huang has resigned, and in his place is a familiar face for anyone that's listened to one of Nvidia's financial calls: it's the company's long-standing CFO, Colette Kress.

But you might be excused as a gamer for never hearing about her; an earnings call isn't everybody's cup of tea.

Colette Kress has been chief financial officer at Nvidia since 2013. That's 13 years sat alongside Jensen in calls with investors and financial institutions to discuss how the company is doing. Kress has been in the role for the record highs of recent years, and the not-so-record lows of others, like the price plummets of '25, '21, and '18.

Prior to her role at Nvidia, Kress was SVP and CFO at Cisco for a couple of years and Corporate VP at Microsoft for nearly five. She also worked at Texas Instruments—all the big hitters, then.

Generally, Kress has stayed out of any contentious issues with the company, only occassionally commenting on the big issues during earnings calls. Like when the RTX 30-series was out of stock everywhere thanks to cryptocurrency mining (the mining had an impact on the company's financials in a slightly contentious way, too).

Or ceaseless comments on the increasing demand for AI datacentre build out. That's of less interest to gamers, but what do you expect? Nvidia to talk about gaming GPUs in this day and age? It cannot be done.

In an email to employees in the wake of Jensen Huang's departure, Kress reportedly said (via Hadas Gold on X):

The PC Gamer Circuit Breaker newsletter breaks down the latest PC gaming tech, and finds you the best deals on the best products

"I believe deeply in this company and in its future. More than anything, I believe in each of you, in our customers and partners and in the vital role we play every day in the global economy.

"The Board, Estaff and I recognize that this has been an extraordinarily difficult period and I want you to know how grateful we are for your resilience, professionalism and continued dedication. Thank you.

"... We play a vital role in building the technology that is powering the AI revolution, and we have important work ahead of us. So let's move forward together, with the same determination and commitment that have always defined this company."

Here are the emails sent to Nvidia employees: Company meeting Nov 18 https://t.co/9X67XzSOCeNovember 12, 2026

Kress also notes there will be a company meeting on November 18—the day after Nvidia's next financial call, which Kress will have been preparing for in her CFO role, and the day of Jensen Huang's meeting with US House leaders.

Kress will have been chosen for this interim CEO role in some part to steady the markets. It takes a long time to find and finalise a deal to secure a new full-time CEO, especially with a job opening as internationally as important as this one. So someone inside the company had to take the chalice for now. With Kress at the helm, Nvidia will be hoping investors won't be quite as worried about the company's financial future.

It's the same playbook we saw when Intel ousted then-CEO Brian Krzanich over a consensual relationship he had with an employee, which was against company policy. Krzanich was replaced by Bob Swan as interim CEO, who actually took over as CEO at a later date, before Pat Gelsinger took over from him in 2021. Pat then retired in 2024.

Nvidia will likely look at this as a bit of a cautionary tale: you want stability and leadership, not a revolving door of top execs and no one steering the ship. If the board has any wits about it, it'll be looking for a strong leader with a clear direction for the company and the will to deliver it.

President Donald Trump has come out in support of a man who only just managed to escape top corporate life at Apple: Tim Cook.

Meanwhile the China Select Committee in US Congress backs any leader that "makes national security its top priority."

So, a true patriot that can also lead teams of top-class engineers and wants to fill the boots of a man that famously didn't take breaks. That'll be easy to find, I'm sure.

#3931. What are we all playing this weekend?

This is the last empty weekend before I go on holiday for a frankly indulgent three weeks. As such, it will likely be spent either remembering all the things my partner and I've not organised for the time we're away or racing to clear through the pile of things I've already remembered I've not organised for the holiday. Whatever the case, it shall not be restful.

Where am I going? Let's just say, I hope to return with some new pairs of glasses and a pair of trainers. If that doesn't give it away, I don't know what will.*

Now, this is what the rest of the team are up to.

EdwinI'm embroiled in helping with a house move again this weekend, so there will be precious little gaming for me. I'd like to fit in a bit more Queen's Domain. I'm happy that the game appears to have caused a stir.

JeremyCastlevania work continues this weekend for our walkthrough, but I'm nearing the finish line. As my anxiety has been pretty bad lately, I will also do my best to catch up on sleep and enjoy time with the wife, as we're both having a very busy end-of-the-year. Dim sum on Sunday afternoon will hopefully be nice.

MarkI must keep my lips shut about what I'll be playing for the majority of this weekend, but if I get any time beyond that I'd like to carry on swan diving my way through Assassin's Creed 3's remaster.

James'Video games? I spit on video games!' James said. 'I would not end my week with such nonsense, not when I could be usefully spending time refining my perpetual motion machine.' Sadly, we all know that's a euphemism for sitting in a rocking chair and eating off-brand Doritos.

OllieI'm gonna return to Marathon for a while, I think. I miss the feel of its maps. But I'll probably need something a bit less stressful to play as well, balance it out a bit. Ooh, maybe this weekend will finally be the weekend I try out Captain Of Industry properly? I've been interested for ages, and recently started watching a Let's Play which has helped me get my bearings a bit.

CallumMarching toward the Treehouse exit in a suit made of tent canvas, Callum announced he was going camping. His jacket sleeves and trouser legs were lined with tentpoles, which made the sight of him trying to climb down the rope ladder an awkward one.

JulianThis weekend I'm playing games that aren't exactly secret – they're all out in the world and playable – but I need to keep them secret from you. You see, I'm trying to play through some of the team's Advent Calendar picks so I can either bolster their vote or try to lobby them to swap them out with one of my faves from the year. I will also be trying to get Crimson Skies working on my PC because I want to once again barrel roll through a canyon in the cockpit of a Hughes P21-J Devastator.

And you, reader dear, what are you playing this weekend…?
